pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/render/src/events.rs:130 The `get_event` Markdown that lt-mcp hands an agent cuts an LLM input/output payload at 4000 chars and marks the cut with a single '…' inside the code fence, without saying how much was dropped or where the rest is. An agent can therefore reason over a clipped payload as if it were whole. The same crate does it properly for spans (traces.rs:89 says 'N of M … truncated'). One caveat: tools.rs also attaches the full body as structuredContent, and whether the model sees it depends on the host.

techniques.evidence: crates/render/src/events.rs:130 The cut marks that it happened but does not name the remainder ('truncation names what it dropped'); jobs.rs:65 repeats the pattern at 1500 chars.

crates/render/src/collective.rs:150 The comment at the attach site names who reads the decoration and why; traces.rs:51 does the same for whole trace ids. Not a full audit: the capabilities table's constant ✅ column was not costed.

crates/render/src/capabilities.rs:19 Tool-level analogue only: the capability view is built from the live backend manifest and puts the refused (501) surfaces first, so an agent is not taught calls the backend rejects.
crates/render/src/lib.rs:105 This is a per-response tool-output renderer, not a prompt stack; there are no identity, policy or task layers to own or order.

pairs.registryProposal: Tool-output producers (MCP renderers) inherit this subject's 'truncation names what it dropped' rule and consumer-coupled-decoration, but context-budgeting is written only for the assembler. A sentence saying the honest-truncation discipline binds every producer whose output lands in model context, or a pointer to tool-result-economy, would remove the ambiguity.
